title: 機器分析化学
subtitle: Instrumental Analytical Chemistry
keywords: Absorption spectrophotometry 2.Optical emission spectrometry 3.Infrared spectroscopy 4.Nuclear magnetic resonance 5.X-ray analysis
educationalGoal: You will learn absorption spectrophotometry for the determination of ions and substances, IR and NMR for structural analysis of organic compounds, X-ray analysis methods, and thermal analysis methods. You will learn the basic principles of each analytical method and the information provided by each method.
advice: You will learn the importance of instrumental analysis in actual analysis. You will learn the basic principles of each analytical method and the information that can be obtained by each analytical method. 1. Role of instrumental analysis 2. Absorption spectrophotometry 3. Atomic absorption spectrometry (AAS) 4. Optical emission spectrometry (OES) 5. X-ray analysis 6. Thermal analysis 7. Infrared spectroscopy (IR) 8. Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR)
books: Textbooks: Unspecified Reference books: Bunseki Kagaku no Kiso (Shokabou Publishing), Kiki Bunseki (Shokabou Publishing), Nyumon Kiki Bunseki Kagaku (Sankyo Shuppan Publishing), Bunseki Kagaku II Bunseki Kagaku (Maruzen Publishing) Reserved books: Kiso Kara Wakaru Kiki Bunseki (Morikita Shuppan Publishing)
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of analytical chemistry, physical chemistry, and organic chemistry is required. Bring a scientific calculator to classes.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand the principles of absorption spectrophotometry.
Be able to understand the principles and characteristics of AAS and OES
Be able to apply IR and NMR to estimate the structure of organic compounds.
Be able to understand the principles and characteristics of X-ray analysis and thermal analysis.

achievementLevels.ideal: Can understand and explain the principles and characteristics of each instrumental analytical method. Can also select the optimum instrumental analytical method to obtain specific information and design an analytical method for it.
achievementLevels.standard: Can understand and explain the principles and characteristics of each instrumental analytical method to some extent. Can also select the optimum instrumental analytical method to obtain specific information and design an analytical method for it after consulting textbooks and other references.

lessons.content: Course outline Importance of instrumental analytical methods Absorption spectrophotometry (1)
lessons.assignments: Preview: The type of instrumental analytical methods Review: Transmittance and absorbance
Preview: Absorbance and transmittance and related calculations Review: Lambert-Beer's law and absorption spectrophotometry
Preview: Absorption spectrophotometry. Review: Principles of atomic absorption spectrometry
Preview: How to create calibration curves Review: Interference in measurements, and concentration calculations using the absolute calibration curve method
Preview: Atomic absorption spectrometry Review: Principles of optical emission spectrometry
Preview: Flame reaction Review: The principles of and differences between ICP-optical emission spectrometry and flame analysis
Preview: Optical emission spectrometry and flame analysis. Review: Types of X-ray analysis and X-ray fluorescent spectroscopy
Preview: The lattice constant and Miller indices Review: X-ray diffraction methods, Bragg's equation and characteristics and principles of thermal analysis
Preview: X-Ray analysis and thermal analysis Review: Principles of infrared spectroscopy
Preview: IR spectra Review: Spectral analysis based on peaks in the IR spectra and characteristic absorption bands
Preview: Infrared spectroscopy Review: The principles of nuclear magnetic resonance
Preview: NMR chemical shifts Review: Chemical shifts and area ratios
Review: spin-spin interactions in NMR spectra Preview: How to analyse NMR spectra
Preview: IR spectra and NMR spectra Review: Complete and submit the exercise
Preview: Nuclear magnetic resonance Review:Identify your mistakes and review your weaknesses.
